topic: Mary Rose (1545): a survivor said she heeled in the wind while turning and water poured through gun ports left open after firing, as Henry VIII watched

research_sources.institution: Calendar of State Papers, Spain, vol. 8: François van der Delft to Charles V, 24 July 1545 (reproduced by All About History)
focus: lowest row of gun ports on one side of the ship

research_cautions: The cause is still debated (gust plus open gunports, overloading, crew indiscipline, a French claim of gunfire); present the survivor's account as one testimony.
Roughly 500 aboard and only about 25-30 survivors per van der Delft; later accounts (Hooker) give 700. The 'sort of knaves' line is a later Carew family account.
The calendar text spells the vice-admiral 'Garew'; he was Sir George Carew.
